sections.h2: What should a seller know about Liberty County, Georgia property tax?
sections.html:
Hinesville anchors Liberty County, which packs in more people per square mile than any other of the four Georgia counties researched here and grew fastest since 2020. Seven taxing areas share the county, each carrying its own proposed rate, so pin down which one your house falls in.

The Census QuickFacts page shows 70,313 residents for July 2025, which is 7.7 percent above the April 2020 base, spread across 516.47 square miles and 126.3 people per square mile at the 2020 count. Owners occupy only 50.9 percent of the housing units, the smallest share in the group. Renters pay a median $1,246, and the typical owned home is valued at $201,500. Builders took out 355 permits in 2025, and 8,042 residents are veterans.

Just 80.7 percent of residents stayed at one address for a year, the lowest figure of the four counties, so moves are common. A house that has been a rental raises questions about its tax history and homestead status, so settle both with the offices below before you list.

The rest of the profile is useful context for pricing. The Census lists 23,998 households averaging 2.70 people, a median household income of $60,456 and a per capita income of $28,215. The civilian labor force takes in 51.8 percent of residents 16 and up, the average commute is 23.9 minutes, and 2022 retail sales reached roughly $873.3 million. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,500 a month.

sections.h2: Which Liberty County office handles my bill, and which my value?
sections.html:
Bills go to the tax commissioner and values to the assessors, and both work out of 100 Main Street in Hinesville. The commissioner's site takes online payments, and the office still accepts them in person or by mail at Suite 1545 (ZIP 31313). Call 912-876-3389.

Assessors work from Suite 1550 at the same address and answer at 912-876-3568. Their handout splits the phone menu this way:

  • Option 1: administration, which covers homesteads and general information.
  • Option 2: mapping, GIS and specialized assessment.
  • Option 3: personal property, including prebill mobile homes, vehicles, boats, business inventory, aircraft and commercial property.
  • Option 4: real property appraisers.

The county's Official Assessment Documents page lets you pull a property record card or a real property assessment notice by typing a parcel number, with a separate search if you do not know yours. The assessors also take email at Tax.Assessors@libertycountyga.gov.

sections.h2: What are the proposed 2026 millage rates in Liberty County?
sections.html:
The county commissioners proposed 19.4000 mills for the unincorporated area and lower rates inside most cities. The figures below come from the county's press release on the proposed 2026 increase, so your bill is the final word on the rate that applies.

Proposed 2026 Liberty County millage rates, per the county press release
AreaProposed county mills
Unincorporated area19.4000
Hinesville17.3350
Flemington17.5590
Walthourville17.7745
Midway17.8746
Riceboro17.8446
Allenhurst and Gumbranch19.4000

The release puts the proposed levy change at 1.32 percent for the unincorporated area and 6.15 percent for Hinesville. Midway and Riceboro show 100 percent only because both set a city rate for the first time in 2026. FLOST, the Floating Local Option Sales Tax, collected from January to June, trims the rollback rates by about 1.6520 mills. Hearings were set for November 3 (noon and 6 p.m.) and November 12, 2026, in the annex board room on North Main Street, and all three dates are behind us.

The release also prints rollback rates, the levels that would raise last year's revenue from the new digest: 19.1460 mills for the unincorporated area, 16.3300 for Hinesville, 17.6830 for Flemington and 18.9030 for Walthourville. Hearings are required wherever a proposal tops its rollback rate. Ask the commissioner for the adopted rate, because your bill will use that figure.

sections.h2: When do Liberty County notices arrive, and what are the appeal rules?
sections.html:
Most notices are mailed in May, and the appeal clock is 45 days from the notice date. The county handout stresses that the notice is no bill, and the exact deadline is printed on it.

The calendar the assessors publish looks like this:

  • Homestead applications and real property returns: January 1 to April 1.
  • Prebill mobile home bills: mailed around February 1, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Annual notices of assessment: mailed in May, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Personal property returns: mailed around December 22 and returned between January 1 and April 1.

Taxes themselves are not qualifying grounds for an appeal. Owners with 10 acres or more of agricultural, forestry or environmentally sensitive land may qualify for a specialized assessment, and the mapping option on the phone menu handles that and any splitting or combining of parcels.

Expect a visit. Staff inspect a property after a homestead application, a return, an appeal, a purchase or a permit, and when it has not been seen in more than three years. They measure, photograph and note features. State code 48-5-264.1 lets appraisers go onto land outside the buildings, and they are expected to carry visible identification.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work for a Liberty County home?
sections.html:
You qualify if you own the land and the home and live in it, and the application deadline is April 1 of each year. Call 912-876-3568 and press 1 to ask what documents to bring.

The state formula takes 40 percent of market value as the assessed figure and subtracts the $2,000 standard exemption before millage applies. Some counties add bigger local amounts, so ask the administration desk about Liberty. Millage differs by area, so the same exemption is worth a different sum in Hinesville than in the unincorporated area.

Your exemption follows you, and the house loses it when you sell. A buyer who will live in the property should file soon after closing, and by April 1 of the first tax year.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes when I sell in Liberty County?
sections.html:
Find out if the year's bill is issued and paid, then settle the split at closing. The January 1 owner answers for the whole year under state rules, and a part-year owner gets nothing back.

The commissioner's online system lets you search records and pay, and a printout can serve as proof of payment for a buyer's lender. With about half of Liberty's units owner-occupied, a tenant may live in the home you are selling. If so, hand the buyer the lease and the tax status together. Call 912-876-3389 about any open balance, and have your closing attorney account for it.

sections.h2: Who lives in Liberty County, and what does that mean for a sale?
sections.html:
Liberty is young. Children under 18 are 27.3 percent of residents, children under 5 are 9.2 percent, and only 11.2 percent are 65 or older. Of adults 25 and up, 92.6 percent finished high school and 20.5 percent hold a bachelor's degree. A share of 6.3 percent were born abroad, and 12.8 percent of residents speak another language at home.

The employer base is sizable: 921 establishments in 2023, total employment of 14,880 with a payroll near $802.6 million, and a 4.5 percent jump in jobs over 2022. With 8,042 veterans in the county, buyers from the military community are part of the market, and an organized tax file helps the paperwork move.

faqs.q: Who values property in Liberty County?
faqs.a: The Liberty County Assessors Office values it, at 100 Main Street, Suite 1550 in Hinesville. Call 912-876-3568 and press 4 to reach the real property appraisers.

faqs.q: When must I file a Liberty County homestead application?
faqs.a: By April 1 each year. Real property returns use the same January 1 to April 1 window.

faqs.q: Does a Liberty County assessment notice demand payment?
faqs.a: No. It explains the appraised and assessed value, and the 45 day appeal period runs from its date.

faqs.q: Where can I view my Liberty County record card?
faqs.a: Type your parcel number into the county's Official Assessment Documents page.

faqs.q: Does sales tax reduce Liberty County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The 2026 release says FLOST receipts from January to June cut the rollback rates by about 1.6520 mills.
